- When sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) and model overpredicts early in the horizon, reduce forecasted values by 1–2% for the first 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by rapid decline, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow for a slight lagged rebound (e.g., +0.5–1.5% in 3–5 days).
- In absence of sentiment signals, model often underestimates mean reversion — apply a 1–3% upward bias in the 10–15 day window to align with observed mean reversion patterns.
- When model forecasts are consistently higher than true outcomes across 30-day horizon, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to the entire forecast sequence, especially if sentiment remains flat.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive signal (e.g., 0.25), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 1–2% in the 3–7 day window following the signal.
